anchor: The Principle of Moments > The Turning Effect of a Single Force > The perpendicular moment arm is always the right-angle distance.
purpose: Show contrast between the true perpendicular moment arm d_perp meeting the force line of action at 90 degrees and an incorrect sloping distance along an angled member.
what_to_show: A diagram showing a force with a vertical line of action, a chosen reference point P, a perpendicular horizontal moment arm labeled d_perp meeting the line of action at a 90-degree right angle marker, and an angled member with a sloping distance that is crossed out.
what_to_notice: The moment arm is strictly the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action, not the distance measured along the sloping beam.

anchor: The Principle of Moments > Formulating and Solving Moment Balance Equations > If the pivot sits at the midpoint, the perpendicular distance to the beam weight is zero.
purpose: Illustrate authentic Cambridge examination problem of a balanced uniform beam on a central knife-edge pivot carrying three discrete masses at different distances.
what_to_show: Authentic Cambridge past-paper diagram showing a uniform 6.0 m beam resting on a central triangular knife-edge pivot at its midpoint, carrying mass A (60 kg) at the left end, mass B (45 kg) at distance x left of the pivot, and mass C (80 kg) at the right end.
what_to_notice: The pivot is located at the center of the beam so the beam weight passes through the pivot and creates zero moment, while clockwise moments from mass C balance anticlockwise moments from masses A and B.

anchor: The Principle of Moments > Strategic Pivot Selection to Eliminate Unknown Forces > The moment produced by that force is therefore zero.
purpose: Demonstrate visually why taking moments about a hinge or pivot point H results in zero moment for an unknown reaction force whose line of action passes through H (d_perp = 0), while showing that the same reaction force has a non-zero moment about any other point Q.
what_to_show: A schematic of a beam hinged at point H with an unknown upward reaction force arrow passing directly through H with d_perp = 0, contrasted with a second reference point Q located away from H where a dashed line shows a non-zero perpendicular distance to the line of action.
what_to_notice: Taking moments about H makes the moment of the hinge reaction force zero because d_perp = 0, removing the unknown from the moment equation without removing the physical force from the system.

anchor: The Principle of Moments > Strategic Pivot Selection to Eliminate Unknown Forces > However, because its moment is zero about that specific point, it drops completely out of your moment balance equation.
purpose: Illustrate authentic Cambridge examination problem of a hinged uniform beam supported by an upward floating cylinder force and carrying a movable person, showing moment arm measurements from the hinge.
what_to_show: Authentic Cambridge diagram of a 6.0 m uniform beam AB hinged at A, supported from below at 5.0 m by a vertical upward force of 1300 N from a floating cylinder, and carrying a person of weight 660 N at variable distance x from hinge A.
what_to_notice: Taking moments about hinge A eliminates the unknown hinge reaction force and sets the anticlockwise moment of the upward cylinder support equal to the clockwise moments of the beam weight and person.

anchor: The Principle of Moments > Multi-Moment Structures and Direct Couple Integration > If a motor applies an anticlockwise torque, you simply add that value to the anticlockwise moment sum.
purpose: Illustrate a complete engineering-style equilibrium setup: a uniform horizontal signboard hinged at a wall, supported by an upward cable at the outer tip, with signboard weight at midpoint and an attached lamp, showing all moment arms measured from the wall hinge.
what_to_show: A horizontal uniform signboard hinged at wall hinge H, showing the downward signboard weight at its center, a downward lamp weight at 3.0 m, and an upward cable tension T at the outer tip 3.6 m from H, with horizontal dimension lines.
what_to_notice: The cable tension acts at a greater perpendicular distance than either downward load, so a smaller tension can balance the combined weights.

anchor: The Principle of Moments > Reaction Forces and the Tipping Threshold > The beam then pivots entirely about the remaining contact point.
purpose: Illustrate authentic Cambridge examination problem of a uniform beam supported on two distinct knife-edge pivots B and C with upward reaction forces FB and FC, demonstrating elimination of FC by taking moments about pivot C and the tipping condition when FB becomes zero.
what_to_show: Authentic Cambridge diagram of a 9.0 m uniform beam AD supported by upward reaction forces FB and FC at pivots B and C (each 2.0 m from the ends), with beam weight 380 N at the center and a 750 N person standing 3.6 m from end D.
what_to_notice: Taking moments about pivot C eliminates reaction force FC to find FB, and tipping occurs when the person moves far enough right that support force FB drops to zero.
